PullRequest.Title: Add configurable xtab reasoning effort and completion token limits
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Add optional `reasoningEffort` and `maxCompletionTokens` fields to the xtab model configuration, including the existing local setting and ExP-driven `modelConfigurationString` / `defaultModelConfigurationString` paths.

Example model configuration:
```json
    "github.copilot.chat.inlineEdits.xtabProvider.modelConfiguration": {
        "modelName": "xxxxxx",
        "promptingStrategy": "patchBased02Unified",
        "includeTagsInCurrentFile": false,
        "maxCompletionTokens": 512,
        "reasoningEffort":"high"
    }
```

**`maxCompletionTokens`** sets `max_completion_tokens`. It is the token limit setting for OpenAI reasoning models. If set, `max_completion_tokens` will replace `max_tokens`.
- Respects `useMaxTokens`. If `useMaxTokens == false`, `max_completion_tokens` is unset.
- Yields to `usePrediction`. If `usePrediction == true`, `max_completion_tokens` is unset

**`reasoningEffort`** simply adds the reasoning effort to the LLM request.

Detailed changes:
- Validate reasoning effort against the OpenAI enum and completion-token limits as finite positive integers.
- Send `reasoning_effort` only when configured.
- When prediction is disabled and `useMaxTokens` is enabled, send configured `max_completion_tokens` instead of `max_tokens`.
- When prediction is enabled, ignore both token-limit controls and retain the existing prediction request behavior.
- Preserve existing requests when the new fields are absent, including model-fallback retries.
- Document the fields in the existing setting description.

## Validation

Commands were run from `extensions/copilot`:

- `npm run test:unit -- xtabPromptOptions.spec.ts inlineEditsModelService.spec.ts xtabProvider.spec.ts chatMLFetcherRetry.spec.ts` — passed, 325 tests, before the final prediction-gating adjustment.
- `npm run test:unit -- xtabProvider.spec.ts -t 'sends model request arguments|only adds configured model request arguments|applies useMaxTokens|retries with default model after NotFound'` — passed, 13 focused tests, after the final adjustment.
- `.\node_modules\.bin\tsc.cmd --noEmit --project tsconfig.json --pretty false` — passed after the final adjustment.
- `npm run compile` — passed after committing the final implementation.
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed before committing.

Manual testing against a local `copilot-proxy` was completed by the author.

## How to Test

1. Run the development extension against a local github-proxy that accepts the two request arguments.
2. Add `reasoningEffort` (for example, `low`) and `maxCompletionTokens` (for example, `8192`) to `github.copilot.chat.inlineEdits.xtabProvider.modelConfiguration`, retaining the model's other configuration fields.
3. With `usePrediction=false` and `useMaxTokens=true`, trigger a next-edit suggestion and verify the serialized body contains `reasoning_effort` and `max_completion_tokens`, but no `max_tokens`.
4. With `useMaxTokens=false`, verify neither token limit is sent.
5. With `usePrediction=true`, verify both token-limit controls are ignored and neither token limit is sent.
6. Remove the new fields and verify existing request behavior remains unchanged.

No linked issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Generate a next-edit suggestion with optional reasoning effort and completion-token configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Model configuration is read from the existing observable selection, prompt construction completes, then one streaming makeChatRequest2 network call must reach first token before edits can be emitted. The diff only adds scalar request fields; model-side reasoning/output work remains on this critical path when explicitly configured.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stream an xtab chat-completions request containing the prompt and optional reasoning_effort/max_completion_tokens.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One network call per normal next-edit attempt, unchanged from before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same path made one streaming request with max_tokens/default prediction behavior; the diff changes two scalar request arguments only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Time to first token blocks edit emission; additional reasoning/output latency is the explicit effect of the newly configured model controls, not accidental repeated client work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One request per debounced next-edit attempt; response work is bounded by the configured maxCompletionTokens and request frequency is governed by the existing typing/debounce/cancellation lifecycle.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The provider keeps the existing cancellation token and streaming request lifecycle. The diff adds no Promise fan-out, queue, or parallel request; superseded attempts remain cancellable as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Selected/default model configurations are held by existing observables. Suggestion responses are not cached; cold and warm attempts each make the same single request, and the diff does not change cache keys or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no client-side multiplicity, serialization growth, or concurrency change was introduced; the traced call path still performs one cancellable request.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact server latency and output size depend on the selected model and explicitly configured effort/token budget.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Higher model compute or a larger response is an intentional, opt-in configuration effect, while absent fields preserve the previous request behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Retry a next-edit suggestion with the default model after a NotFound response
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selected-model request must fail with NotFound before doGetNextEdit issues the default-model request; both sequential network calls are on the suggestion critical path only in this existing fallback case.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue the selected-model request and, only after NotFound, retry using the default model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two sequential calls in the NotFound case, the same cardinality as before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: NotFound already triggered one default-model retry; the changed code only sends the corresponding model configuration fields on each existing call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both calls delay suggestion completion in the fallback case, but no extra call or retry condition is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most two requests for one suggestion attempt: selected model plus one default-model fallback. The existing forceUseDefaultModel guard prevents an unbounded retry loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fallback is sequential after the first response, not concurrent. The diff only carries each attempt's own selected/default configuration into its request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No response cache participates. The provider's existing forceUseDefaultModel state bounds subsequent fallback behavior; the diff does not alter that lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the fallback branch and one-retry guard are unchanged and tests demonstrate the same two calls with different existing model selections.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: NotFound prevalence and network duration are deployment-dependent, but request cardinality and sequencing are explicit in the code.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression because the diff neither adds a retry nor increases fallback concurrency/cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load local or experiment-driven xtab model configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing treatment readiness and, when slash-model discovery is required, model-list loading complete before model selection. Validation and propagation of the two new scalar fields occur in the existing observable recomputation path, not per streamed token.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the proxy model list when existing slash-model selection requires discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced load for the active token in normal operation; retries only if the token changes, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same treatment/model discovery path ran before this change; only accepted configuration properties differ.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can block initial model selection, but the new configuration fields neither introduce nor move this existing load.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A small model configuration object on setting/treatment/model-list changes; model discovery is coalesced by token and cached once loaded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing TaskQueue and refresh task singler serialize/coalesce model selection and model-list loading. The diff does not add asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The model service recomputes from cached observables; proxy model discovery returns immediately when modelsLoaded is true and coalesces in-flight refreshes by token. New fields do not affect these keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that validation adds only constant work during existing observable recomputation and no new boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether discovery runs depends on existing slash-model configuration and warm model state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup or configuration-path regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all nine changed files and traced request serialization, streaming, cancellation, NotFound fallback, configuration observables, and model discovery. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found.
